name: Record when staff arrive and leave, and correct a wrong record under approval
priorityReason: This record determines pay. An error in it is a wage paid wrongly, not a reporting inconvenience.

goal.capability: to record staff attendance and have a wrong record corrected under approval
goal.outcome: payroll runs on a record that is accurate and that nobody could quietly change in their own favour

secondaryActors.involvement: Are the subjects of the record, and may check themselves in where the geofence is enabled.
Approves corrections, and marks or corrects the School Admin's own attendance.
Reads the month's record for payroll and cannot amend it.

additional.description: The month closes and the record is passed to payroll (BR-11).
A geofence check-in arrives from a staff member's device, where that is enabled.

preconditions.condition: Staff records exist for the people being marked.
An authenticated session exists and the acting user is School Admin or Principal.
The off-day and holiday calendar is set for the month, so a day off is coded as such rather than as an absence.
Approved staff leave for the date is available, so a day on sanctioned leave is not coded absent.

postConditions: Every staff member carries a code for the day — present, absent, leave, day-off or holiday — with a time in and, where recorded, a time out.
The School Admin's own attendance was marked or corrected by the Principal, never by themselves.
Any correction carries the person who raised it, the person who approved it, the reason and the date, and the original entry stays visible alongside the corrected one.
No correction took effect without the Principal's approval, because this record determines pay.
The month's record is available to payroll, which reads it and cannot amend it.
A day off or a holiday is coded as such and is not counted as an absence against anybody.
The Super Admin holds no authority over any attendance record and could not have changed one.

actions: Select the corrected code and times

dataFields.name: Time out
dataFields.validation: When they left. Recorded later in the day and may be left blank (BR-4).

dataFields.name: Code
dataFields.validation: How the day is treated. Payroll reads this (BR-3).

dataFields.name: Source
dataFields.validation: How the record arose, which matters when it is questioned.

dataFields.name: Correction reason
dataFields.validation: 20 to 500 characters. Mandatory, since this record determines pay (BR-6).
dataFields.example: Was on a school trip to the science fair; the register was not marked that day.

dataFields.name: Approved by
dataFields.validation: The Principal. No other role can approve (BR-7).

dataFields.name: Payable days
dataFields.validation: Days the month's record makes payable, derived from the codes rather than typed (BR-11).

entities.notes: One per staff member per date, with its times and code. Never deleted.
One per correction, with its reason, raiser and approver. Takes effect only on approval (BR-7).
Read for the people being marked and their departments.
Read so a day on approved leave is coded Leave rather than Absent (BR-9).
Read so a day off or holiday is coded as such (BR-8).
Every mark, every correction raised and every approval.

permissions.rowScope: Own branch; may switch per branch-scope.
permissions.notes: Marks staff attendance and raises corrections. Cannot approve a correction, and cannot mark or correct their own record (BR-5, BR-7).
Approves corrections, and marks or corrects the School Admin's own attendance (BR-5).
Reads the month's record for payroll and cannot amend it (BR-10).
Sees their own attendance and may check themselves in where the geofence is enabled. Cannot change a record.

permissions.rowScope: No authority over any attendance record (BR-12).

businessRules.rule: The School Admin marks staff attendance. Where a check-in is missing or a device has failed, the record is still made by hand rather than left blank.
A record carries a time in and, later in the day, a time out. The two are entered at different moments and a missing time out does not invalidate the day.
Every day is coded present, absent, leave, day-off or holiday. Payroll reads the code, so an uncoded day is a day nobody can be paid for.
A time out may be left blank where somebody left without it being recorded. The day is still coded, and the gap is visible rather than guessed at.
The School Admin's own attendance is marked and corrected by the Principal. The person who marks should not be the person who corrects their own record.
A correction carries a written reason. This record determines pay, and a change to it with no explanation is the thing an auditor asks about first.
A correction takes effect only when the Principal approves it. The School Admin raises it; they do not grant it.
A day off or a holiday is coded as such and is never counted as an absence. The off-day calendar decides which days those are.
A day on approved leave is coded Leave, not Absent. The two are treated differently by payroll and by any disciplinary process.
Accounts read the record for payroll and cannot amend it. The role that calculates pay must not be the role that sets the days it is calculated from.
The month's record feeds the payroll calculation, and the payable days are derived from the codes rather than entered separately.
The Super Admin holds no authority over attendance records. A technical administrator is not a person who decides what somebody is paid.
The original entry stays visible alongside the corrected one. A corrected record shows what it was as well as what it became.

transitions.condition: The day is coded and the times recorded (BR-1, BR-3).
A correction is raised with a reason (BR-6).
The correction is approved and takes effect (BR-7).
The correction is returned. The original record stands.

basicFlow.userAction: Marks staff attendance for the day, entering the time in and coding the day.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Records the entry, codes the day, and refuses to mark the acting user's own record.

basicFlow.userAction: Records the time out later in the day.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Adds the time out to the existing record without changing its code.
Codes a day off or a holiday as such, and a day on approved leave as Leave rather than Absent.

basicFlow.userAction: Raises a correction where a record is wrong, stating the reason.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Holds the correction pending approval. The original record still stands in the meantime.

basicFlow.userAction: Reviews the correction and approves it.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Applies the corrected record, keeps the original visible alongside it, and records who raised and who approved.

basicFlow.userAction: Marks or corrects the School Admin's own attendance.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Records it, since the person who marks should not correct their own record.
Passes the month's record to payroll, with payable days derived from the codes. Accounts read it and cannot amend it.

alternateFlows.condition: A self check-in arrives from a staff member's device
alternateFlows.behaviour: The record is created from the check-in with its source noted. Where the geofence is not enabled or the device has failed, the School Admin marks it by hand instead (BR-1).
The day is still coded and the missing time out is visible rather than guessed at (BR-4).

alternateFlows.condition: The staff member is on approved leave
alternateFlows.behaviour: The day is coded Leave rather than Absent, since the two are treated differently by payroll and by any disciplinary process (BR-9).

alternateFlows.condition: The Principal does not accept the correction
alternateFlows.navigation: Attendance corrections → Return with a reason
alternateFlows.behaviour: The original record stands and the correction does not take effect. Nothing about the day has changed (BR-7).

alternateFlows.condition: The record to be corrected is the School Admin's own
alternateFlows.navigation: Login → Attendance → Staff attendance → Raise correction
alternateFlows.behaviour: The Principal raises and applies it. The School Admin cannot correct their own record at all (BR-5).

alternateFlows.condition: Accounts need the month for payroll
alternateFlows.behaviour: They read the record and the payable days derived from it. There is no control that lets them change a code (BR-10).

exceptions.condition: The School Admin attempts to approve their own correction
exceptions.messageShown: Only the Principal can approve an attendance correction.

exceptions.messageShown: The time out cannot be before the time in.

departures.requirement: Marking, correcting and approving are three separate hands, and nobody can mark or correct their own record. Accounts read but never write.
The original entry is retained alongside every corrected one, with the raiser, the approver and the reason. This record determines pay.
Payable days are derived from the codes and are never entered separately, so the two cannot disagree.
Staff attendance and its corrections are retained 7 years, matching payroll records.

openQuestions.question: Does the school expect self check-in at launch, or is manual marking the only route?
openQuestions.assumption: Manual marking is the workflow given; the geofence is a later phase.

openQuestions.question: What counts as late, and does it affect pay?
openQuestions.assumption: Not specified, though the monthly report shows a late count.

openQuestions.question: Who marks the Principal's own attendance?
openQuestions.assumption: Not specified. The chain stops at the Principal correcting the School Admin.

openQuestions.question: What happens to pay when a correction is approved after payroll has run for that month?
openQuestions.assumption: Flagged as needing an adjustment, but the adjustment route is not specified.

openQuestions.question: Should a half day be a code of its own, or handled as leave?
openQuestions.assumption: Not specified, and schools commonly need one.

conventionsApplied.name: session-and-authentication
conventionsApplied.rule: Every use case except the login use case assumes an authenticated session. Sign out is available on every screen. An expired or invalid session returns the user to the login screen with the message "Your session has ended. Please sign in again."

conventionsApplied.name: role-based-access
conventionsApplied.rule: Access is enforced server-side on every request, not only by hiding menu items. A request for a record outside the actor's permitted scope returns a 403 and the message "You do not have permission to view this record." A use case states additions and restrictions only.

conventionsApplied.name: branch-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every record carries a branch ID. Users see only their own branch unless the use case states otherwise. Super Admin, School Admin and Principal may switch branch from the header.

conventionsApplied.name: list-screens
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list supports search, column sort and page-size selection. Default page size 25; default sort is most recent first. Filters are applied before printing or exporting.

conventionsApplied.name: print-and-pdf
conventionsApplied.rule: Every report and list offers Print and Download as PDF, honouring the filters currently applied. Each output carries the school name, branch, academic session, report title, filter summary, generation timestamp and the name of the user who generated it.

conventionsApplied.name: audit-trail
conventionsApplied.rule: Every create, update, deactivation, approval and reversal writes to the audit log: actor, role, timestamp, record type, record ID, before and after values, and IP address. Audit entries are never editable.

conventionsApplied.name: deletion
conventionsApplied.rule: Records are deactivated, not physically removed. Deactivated records are excluded from lists and lookups but remain in the audit trail and in historical reports. A record referenced by a financial transaction can never be deactivated.

conventionsApplied.name: validation-and-messages
conventionsApplied.rule: Field-level errors appear inline beneath the field on blur and on submit. Errors that block the whole action appear as a banner at the top of the form. Successful actions show a toast. No action succeeds silently.

conventionsApplied.name: dates-times-numbers
conventionsApplied.rule: Dates display as DD-MM-YYYY; date and time as DD-MM-YYYY HH:mm in 24-hour form. Times are school-local. Phone numbers are stored in the registered mobile format.

conventionsApplied.name: language
conventionsApplied.rule: All user-visible strings come from a resource file. No hard-coded text in any screen.

conventionsApplied.name: concurrency-and-locking
conventionsApplied.rule: Last write wins, except where a use case defines an approval lock. Once a record is approved, posted or issued it becomes read-only and can only be changed through its defined reversal use case.

conventionsApplied.name: screen-states
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list, dashboard tile and report defines four states: loading, empty, error and populated. The empty state names what is missing and links to the action that creates it.

conventionsApplied.name: notifications
conventionsApplied.rule: All outbound SMS, WhatsApp, email and push messages are sent through the Messaging module, recorded in the sent-message log with per-channel delivery status, and use a named template. Use cases reference the template; they do not embed message text.

conventionsApplied.name: default-performance-and-retention
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise: a screen loads within 2 seconds and a save completes within 2 seconds at 200 concurrent users; lists paginate above 100 rows; financial and student records are retained 7 years; audit and message logs 12 months; every screen is usable at a 360 px viewport. Fill the non-functional field only to depart from this.

conventionsApplied.name: default-trigger
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise, the trigger is: the user navigates to the screen and initiates the action. Fill the Triggers field only where a scheduled job, an event in another module, or an inbound external call also starts it.
